title: Self Referential System
definition: A system that uses its own output as input, creating a circular feedback loop for continuous adaptation and understanding.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine trying to take a picture of yourself with a camera. To do it, you need the camera. So, you build a camera and use it to take a picture of yourself, and then use that picture to build a better camera, and so on. This is similar to what we're doing with the Hieros Network.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A self-referential system is a recursive process where the output of a system becomes the input for the same system. This concept is central to complex systems theory and the philosophy of science, as it highlights the interconnectedness of observation and manipulation. The Hieros Network is an embodiment of this idea, as its design allows it to both observe and shape the systems it studies.
difficulty_levels.expert: The self-referential system presents a philosophical challenge to classical notions of observation and causality. By incorporating the observer into the system, it challenges the idea of an objective reality and suggests that knowledge is constructed through a continuous process of interaction with the environment. This concept has implications for various fields, including philosophy of language, epistemology, and the nature of consciousness.

extra_fields.insight: The Hieros Network is not only a tool for understanding complex systems; it is a manifestation of the self-referential system itself. By designing and studying the network simultaneously, we are part of the experiment and the mirror.
